thread:
ajay: Heads-up — RFC follow-up: proposing a lightweight polyfill + circuit-breaker approach for v4->v5 API migrations. want quick sanity check before i write the rollout doc.

maria: +1, can you sketch the failure modes you're trying to cover?

ajay: sure. two main concerns: 1) new required fields breaking older clients, 2) partial runtime incompat (streaming vs non-streaming) causing errors or latency spikes. polyfill handles missing new fields; circuit-breaker routes to v4 when the runtime reports degradation.

tom: how is this different from the existing compat-shim? sounds similar.

ajay: good q. compat-shim today is heavier (request proxy + translation). this polyfill is inline in the edge router — cheaper & faster. it's opt-in per-tenant and uses a short-lived runtime health signal instead of full translation.

sophia: i worry about semantics: if we polyfill new fields, we might produce inconsistent outputs vs clients that actually send them. is that ok?

ajay: yeah that's a tradeoff. polyfill chooses safe defaults (e.g., temperature=0.7, truncated max_tokens), but we log a "polyfill_applied" tag so evals can filter those calls. goal is availability not exact parity.

elaine: what about authorization/telemetry? we need clear signals for deprecation metrics.

ajay: plan: add header `x-rw-migration-state: polyfilled|passed|bypassed` on responses, and increment telemetry counter `compat.polyfill.v5_applied`. also capture client version tag when present.

samir: circuit-breaker details? thresholds?

ajay: simple start: trip when p95 latency to v5 runtime > 750ms for 30s OR error-rate > 2% for 1m. when tripped, router serves v4 for 2m then re-probes. we can tune.

maria: can we test locally? example request + header?

ajay: yep, here's the short curl we used in staging: ```bash
curl -X POST https://edge.internal/rpc \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rw-v5", "prompt":"hello", "client_version":"4.2.1"}'
```

ajay: router pseudo-check (edge) 
```js
if (!req.body.hasOwnProperty('new_feature_flag')) {
  req.headers['x-rw-migration-state']='polyfilled';
  req.body.new_feature_flag = false;
}
if (runtimeHealth(v5).degraded) routeTo('v4');
```

tom: sounds reasonable. what about KV cache mismatch when we fall back to v4? tokens and cache keys might differ.

ajay: important. fallback includes a cache-warm header to avoid cold-start penalties: `x-rw-cache-warm: <hash-of-canonical-prompt>` and router will attempt to fetch compatible cache keys. if not found we accept higher latency for first requests.

sophia: we should add an eval suite to detect behavioral drift introduced by polyfills. we can tie alerts to >1% regression on customer prompt sets.

ajay: agreed — action item: @sophia to author a small eval harness and a regression threshold for rollout gating.

sophia: taking it. timeline?

ajay: propose phases: 1) internal canary (engineering tenants) for 48h, 2) invited customers opt-in flag for 2 weeks, 3) gradual auto-rollout for low-traffic tenants, 4) full roll once metrics look stable.

elaine: who owns infra work for the router changes?

ajay: infra owns routing + circuit-breaker (tom + infra oncall). sophia owns evals, maria owns telemetry dashboard, samir will draft the migration doc + customer comms.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline check: edge-router branch `polyfill/edge-circuit-breaker` passes unit tests. staging deploy queued.

maria: one more nit — we should expose an opt-out header `x-rw-compat-optout: true` so customers can opt out of polyfills if they prefer hard errors.

ajay: good call, will add. default = opt-in=false (we don't polyfill unless tenant opt-in) for initial rollout.

tom: ok to proceed drafting the RFC/rollout doc. pls include a section on billing implications (polyfilled calls still bill as v5?)

ajay: yes — billing note: polyfilled calls counted as v5 but annotated in telemetry for cost analysis. may change later.

samir: i'll start the migration doc PR after lunch. tagging owners in the draft.

maria: :thumbsup: add runbook for when circuit-breaker oscillates (flapping) — do not auto-escalate until 15min sustained.

ajay: good. thanks everyone — i'll post the RFC link when PR is up.
